display_title: Google Updates Policy on AI Data and Advertising
display_title_he: גוגל מעדכנת את מדיניות הפרטיות לגבי נתוני בינה מלאכותית ופרסום
short_summary: Google has updated its privacy terms to allow data from Gmail, Drive, and Photos to influence personalized advertisements when linked to AI features.

sources.name: The Verge
sources.title: Now Google says it might use your Gmail and Google Photos data to target ads

sources.name: Ars Technica
sources.title: Updated Google privacy policy says your Gmail might be used for advertising

paragraphs: For years, Google maintained a relatively unambiguous boundary between users' personal storage and its lucrative advertising network. In its ad personalization rules, the tech giant explicitly assured consumers that it would not serve personalized advertisements based on material stored inside Google Drive, Gmail, or Google Photos. However, an update made quietly to its privacy policy on October 16 has modified that longstanding stance. The change, initially spotted by Android Authority, introduces subtle language caveats that allow personal data to influence commercial targeting under specific circumstances.

While the primary prohibition remains technically intact, Google has appended a decisive exception to the text: content will not be exploited for personalized ads "unless you choose to make data from these services available to other Google services that support personalized ads." In practice, this equivocation opens the door for Workspace applications and photo libraries to inform marketing systems. This regulatory bridge is anchored by Personal Intelligence, a feature launched in early 2026 designed to link multiple applications directly to Google AI products, including the Gemini app and Search tools like AI Mode.

Google's overarching ambition is to allow its diverse ecosystem of products and services to communicate seamlessly, regarding user data as a vital asset for refining artificial intelligence. When users link their inboxes, photo archives, and cloud documents, AI tools draw on added context to generate richer answers and personalized recommendations. However, this cross-service sharing proves to be a privacy minefield. While the standalone Gemini application currently remains ad-free, AI Mode functions inside Search, where sponsored content and promotional results are commonplace.

Addressing the scrutiny, Google issued a statement emphasizing that connecting applications remains entirely opt-in. The company clarified that promotional messages will continue to reflect user queries, dialogue context, and established general interests, insisting that ads will not be based "directly" on inbox contents or photo galleries, nor will sensitive information ever tailor ads. According to the revised policy, however, when Search receives permission to access Workspace or Photos data, it can process that information to customize content, including advertising. The company notes, for instance, that searching for mountain bikes might generate sports equipment advertisements on YouTube.

Privacy observers caution that while the integration is optional, Google actively employs pop-ups and interface prompts to entice users to activate Personal Intelligence without completely outlining the promotional ramifications. Furthermore, interactions fed into AI systems could pose broader data challenges, given that user inputs and model outputs help train machine learning systems, even if Google attempts to filter personal information out of training sets.

For individuals seeking to prevent their private files from influencing advertisements, manual adjustments are necessary. Users can disable connected applications through the Gemini interface or navigate through their Google account under Data & privacy to manage connected content apps within Search Services personalization settings. Disconnecting Workspace apps and Google Photos ensures personal data remains quarantined from promotional algorithms.

facts.fact: On October 16, Google updated its privacy policy, adding an exception to its longstanding rule against using data from Gmail, Drive, or Google Photos for ad targeting.

The policy previously barred personalized ads based on Drive, Gmail, or Photos, but now allows it if users make data from these services available to other Google services supporting personalized ads.
The policy change was originally spotted by Android Authority.
Earlier in 2026, Google launched Personal Intelligence, letting users connect Workspace apps and Photos to AI products like Gemini and AI Mode in Search.
While the Gemini application does not currently feature advertisements, Search and AI Mode do include sponsored content.
Google stated that connecting apps is entirely opt-in, ads will not be based directly on inboxes or photo libraries, and sensitive information is not used to tailor ads.
Users can revoke access or prevent their personal data from informing ads by disconnecting apps or disabling personalized recommendations in their Google account settings.
